decisions.reason: The award signal and close fit with the firm's existing organic dairy range make this a low-cost option with encouraging early evidence, so management would likely keep it on the market.
Its home-page promotion suggests strategic support and the product extends an established cheese line, so the firm would likely continue it while demand becomes clearer.
This semi-hard cheese wheel fits the core business and should be relatively cheap to keep, but the lack of any stronger success signal raises some risk of later pruning.
The spicy cheese is still a plausible low-cost adjacent option, yet with only a basic mention and several similar cheese launches the firm would keep it cautiously rather than commit strongly.
As a clearly introduced new soft cheese variant close to the established assortment, it likely merits more time on the market before the firm would abandon the option.

Although it leverages existing cheese capabilities, washed-rind soft cheese is somewhat more niche and lacks visible positive feedback, so it is the most exposed to future rationalization but still worth keeping for now.
